title: Till Eulenspiegel.
lines: Long ago, in Flanders, there lived a boy called Till.
He lived in Damme, a little town close to Bruges.
Till always wore a hat with two points, and on each point hung a little bell.
Ting-a-ling, it went when he walked.
And Till always had an owl and a mirror with him.
An owl, because owls are clever.
And a mirror, so people could take a good look at themselves.
But his jokes were never mean to poor people.
He mostly played tricks on rich people and show-offs.
People who thought they were better than others.
One day Till came to a town where a very stingy baker lived.
The baker baked the tastiest bread.
But he never gave anything to the poor children who stood outside his shop.
He chased them away with his broom.
Good day, baker, he said politely.
I work for a rich gentleman.
He wants a big sack full of bread.
He filled a big sack with loaves.
But on the way he secretly made a little hole in the sack.
Out of the hole fell the loaves, one by one, onto the street.
When Till was at the door, he called: Oh dear, baker!
The rich gentleman has no money with him.
Till pointed to the street, where the children were tucking in.
It's with people who were hungry, he said.
And I think you did a good deed today, baker.
Do you know how good that feels?
At first the baker was angry.
But then he looked at the children.
Something happened in the baker's heart.
Till held his mirror up to the baker's face.
From that day on the baker gave the bread he hadn't sold to the children every evening.
He came to a castle where a lord lived who was very proud of his beautiful paintings.
Till said he was a painter.
I'll make the most beautiful painting you've ever seen, he said.
But only clever people can see it.
Till sat in a room for a week.
Then he showed the lord an empty wall.
But he didn't want to look silly.
Everyone in the castle said the same.
Until a little girl came in.
Till laughed so hard that his bells jingled.
The girl is right, he said.
Always dare to say what you see, even when others say something different.
But then he had to laugh too.
Till Eulenspiegel travelled around for a long time, with his owl, his mirror and his hat with bells.
And in Damme there is still a statue of him today.
When you look at it, it seems as if he's winking at you.
